title: Investigate and fix metering pipeline for streaming and token accounting edge cases
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Summary:
We are seeing a class of customer-reported discrepancies between billed token usage and what users observe client-side for streaming generation and edge-case flows (cancellations, retries, partial flushes, and function-calling responses). The goal of this ticket is to audit the end-to-end metering pipeline, identify and fix sources of double-counting, under-counting, and non-deterministic counts for streaming requests, and add robust tests and observability so regressions are detectable and actionable.

Background and motivation:
- Billing accuracy is critical; even small systematic errors (1-2%) cause customer trust issues and large revenue drift.
- Streaming responses are metered differently from non-streaming: we currently emit provisional events per-chunk and commit a final count at completion. This mixed model has produced mismatches when sessions are aborted, retried, or when the runtime downstream applies truncation/safety filters.
- Common customer-facing symptoms: billed tokens > client count (duplicate counting on retries), billed tokens < client count (truncation not reflected), and inconsistent per-route totals in daily reports.

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: token counting correctness for text generation and chat endpoints (streaming and non-streaming), idempotency and retry semantics, commit/rollback semantics for streaming, interaction with rate-limiter provisional counters, and metrics/dashboards.
- Out of scope: embedding billing is handled by a separate flow (ENG-4135), storage of raw audio tokens, and 3rd-party reseller billing reconciliation (handles later).
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline produces deterministic final token counts for streaming and non-streaming requests when given the same input and idempotency key.
Retries (identical idempotency key) do not create double billing; if a retry succeeds after a failure the total billed tokens equals the single logical request's final count.
Aborted/cancelled streams are billed only for committed tokens per defined policy (see technical_notes).
Edge cases where runtime truncates or inserts assistant function-calls are reflected exactly in final committed counts.
Automated unit and integration tests cover: chunk-level accounting, partial flush + abort, network duplicate events, and rate-limit preemption scenarios.
Dashboard alerts and a nightly reconciliation job detect >0.5% drift relative to aggregated tokenizer-based baseline for production traffic in the canary fleet.
A documented migration/rollout plan to flip fixes to prod behind a canary toggle and to recover from any unexpected billing deltas.
technical_notes:
Current pipeline overview:
1) Edge proxy receives request and assigns request_id + idempotency_key (when provided).
2) Streaming chunks are forwarded to the runtime; per-chunk token-estimates are emitted to the provisional meter via a lightweight API (provisional_counter.increment).
3) On completion the runtime posts a final summary with exact token counts (input_tokens, output_tokens, prompt_trimmed_tokens, truncated_tokens) to the aggregator which writes a committed record to the usage store.
4) Billing jobs aggregate committed records per customer.

Observed failure modes and proposed fixes:
- Duplicate provisional events on partial network retries: add per-request provisional idempotency (provisional_event_id) and dedupe on the aggregator for a given request_id.
- Retries that re-run generation create provisional and committed events twice when idempotency_key is missing: make idempotency_key required for clients that enable client-side retries (or automatically attach a server-side generated idempotency token for retryable pathways).
- Aborts mid-stream: current behavior bills all provisional increments. Change behavior to mark provisional increments as 'tentative' and only convert to committed on final summary. Implement a time-windowed garbage collector to expire tentative increments after X minutes and ensure they are not billed.
- Function-calls and structured output: the runtime sometimes emits assistant chunks with nested function payloads which the chunk-based tokenizer estimate undercounts due to JSON overhead. The final summary must re-run the canonical tokenizer on the serialized final output and override any provisional sums.
- Rate limiter interplay: rate limiter currently decrements available quota when provisional increments occur to prevent bursts. Modify to use 'reserved' quota units that are reconciled/committed on finalization so temporary provisional usage does not permanently reduce quota on aborted requests.

Design decisions and justifications:
- Commit-time canonicalization: final committed counts must be computed by a single service (aggregator) applying the canonical tokenizer and model-specific rules so all customers see consistent results.
- Tentative->committed workflow prevents over-billing for aborted streams while still allowing rate-limiter guardrails.
- Idempotency and dedupe: primary defense against double-billing is to require dedupe-key for clients that may retry; for legacy flows add server-side generated ids and best-effort dedupe for a recovery window.
testing_plan: Unit tests: chunk accounting module with randomized chunk boundaries and tokenizer outputs.

Integration tests: end-to-end streaming scenario using test runtime that simulates partial flush, mid-stream aborts, duplicates, and function-calls. Verify final committed counts match the canonical tokenizer baseline.

Property/fuzz tests: randomized interleaving of provisional events + final summaries; assert monotonicity and bounded divergence (<1 token) between aggregator computed final count and re-tokenized final text.
Replay tests: reprocess production-like gzipped request traces in a staging aggregator to verify no historical edge-case double-counting.
Load tests: exercise rate-limiter reconciliation under sustained streaming traffic to validate reserved quota behavior and ensure no regressions in latency.
Nightly reconciliation job: compare per-request committed counts against a separate tokenization baseline for sampled traffic to detect regressions after deploy.
observability_and_metrics:
Add the following metrics and tags: 
- meter.provisional_events.count (by model, route, request_source)
- meter.commits.count and meter.commits.tokens_total (histogram by model + plan tier)
- meter.dedupe.dropped_events (counts where dedupe prevented double increment)
- meter.gc.tentative_expirations (number of tentative increments expired)
- meter.reconciliation.drift (daily % drift per customer sample)
- logs: trace per request_id containing all provisional events and final summary for fast root cause.
Also add an alert: daily_reconciliation_drift > 0.5% for 12 hours triggers PagerDuty to SRE and Billing PM.
rollout_plan: Merge fix behind feature-flag in billing-aggregator and deploy to canary cluster (10% traffic) for 48 hours.
Run replay job on canary: validate zero net increase in billed tokens outside expected variance for sampled customers.
If canary stable, ramp to 50% with additional monitoring, then to 100% after 72 hours.
Communication: pre-rollout customer advisory for enterprise customers with reserved capacity and billing contacts; post-rollout incident report if >0.5% delta observed.
Backout: revert feature-flag and run reconciliation to normalize any interim tentative increments if a rollback is necessary.
